candidates.name: The Lord of the Rings: Fate of the Fellowship
candidates.description: Guide the Fellowship through Middle-earth's perils, where every choice echoes the weight of fate and the Ring's corruption.
candidates.justification: M(4): Action points, variable powers, and multi-use cards create tactical depth. T(5): Every corruption track and heroic moment IS living Tolkien's epic. G(4): Narrative choices and fellowship management carry enormous thematic weight. F(2): Campaign setup and multiple systems add moderate overhead. Ar(5): Stunning Middle-earth artwork captures Jackson's cinematic vision perfectly.

candidates.name: Moon Colony Bloodbath
candidates.description: Survive the horrors lurking in a moon colony where oxygen runs low and something unspeakable stalks the corridors.
candidates.justification: M(4): Action points with asymmetric powers and escalating scenario complexity. T(5): Oxygen depletion and stalking horror mechanics generate genuine dread. G(4): Every action point spent carries life-or-death consequences. F(2): Scenario setup and component management add moderate overhead. Ar(4): Atmospheric sci-fi horror aesthetic with strong thematic cohesion.

candidates.name: Lands of Evershade
mechs: CAR-04 Card Draw, Limits, and Deck Exhaustion
candidates.description: Delve into cursed shadow realms where light itself becomes a precious resource and ancient evils stir in the perpetual twilight.
candidates.justification: M(4): Action points with evolving character abilities and multi-layered shadow mechanics. T(5): Light-as-resource and shadow corruption mechanics generate mounting dread perfectly. G(4): Every move into darkness creates meaningful risk-reward tension. F(2): Campaign setup and multiple component types add overhead. Ar(4): Atmospheric twilight artwork creates perfect gothic mood.

candidates.name: Revenant
mechs: CAR-04 Card Draw, Limits, and Deck Exhaustion
candidates.description: Return from death as a vengeful spirit to hunt down your killer while your corporeal form decays with each passing hour.
candidates.justification: M(4): Action points with supernatural powers, investigation mechanics, and time pressure systems. T(5): Playing as undead spirit with decay timer generates existential horror perfectly. G(4): Meaningful choices balancing investigation speed against spiritual deterioration consequences. F(2): Campaign setup and multiple card decks create moderate overhead. Ar(4): Atmospheric gothic horror art with strong character design.

candidates.name: Fate: Defenders of Grimheim
candidates.description: Channel the power of Fate itself to defend the last bastion of hope against an encroaching darkness that devours worlds.
candidates.justification: M(4): Fate Core mechanics with aspects, stunts, and multi-use cards create tactical depth. T(5): Invoking aspects and compels IS wielding narrative fate magic against darkness. G(4): Every aspect invocation and fate point spend reshapes story outcomes meaningfully. F(2): Campaign setup and fate point tracking add moderate overhead between sessions. Ar(4): Dark fantasy aesthetic with atmospheric character and location art throughout.

candidates.name: Halls of Hegra
candidates.description: Outnumbered Norwegian defenders make their last stand against overwhelming German forces in a doomed fortress siege.
candidates.justification: M(4): Action points with event deck and dice combat create tactical depth. T(5): Every action IS the desperate last stand - you feel doomed heroism. G(4): Meaningful choices about resource allocation and defensive positioning under pressure. F(2): Solo setup and rulebook density manageable but not trivial. Ar(4): Atmospheric WWII art captures Norwegian fortress and winter desperation perfectly.

candidates.name: Wroth
mechs: CAR-04 Card Draw, Limits, and Deck Exhaustion
VIC-02 Victory Points from Player Actions
candidates.description: Lead survivors through a cursed wasteland where every step forward risks awakening ancient horrors that hunger for your sanity.
candidates.justification: M(4): Action points with variable powers and multi-use cards create tactical depth. T(5): Curse mechanics and sanity loss generate genuine dread and desperation. G(4): Every action carries meaningful risk-reward tension in hostile environment. F(2): Setup and card management add overhead but remain manageable. Ar(4): Dark atmospheric art captures apocalyptic horror tone effectively.

candidates.name: Dune: Imperium – Uprising
mechs: VIC-01 Victory Points from Game State
VIC-02 Victory Points from Player Actions
candidates.description: Navigate the deadly politics of Arrakis as a Great House leader, wielding spice, influence, and betrayal to claim the Imperial throne.
candidates.justification: M(4): Deck-building with worker placement creates deep interlocking systems and combos. T(3): Political maneuvering feels right but mechanics reference more than generate Dune. G(4): Every card and worker placement cascades into meaningful strategic consequences. F(2): Setup and iconography density manageable but requires rules investment. Ar(4): Stunning desert palette and character art captures Dune's epic scope.

candidates.name: Stupor Mundi
mechs: VIC-01 Victory Points from Game State
candidates.description: Lead medieval kingdoms through political intrigue, crusades, and cultural renaissance in the age of Frederick II.
candidates.justification: M(4): Area control with asymmetric powers, tech trees, and multiple victory paths. T(3): Medieval politics theme present but mechanics don't fully embody it. G(4): Meaningful strategic choices across military, diplomatic, and cultural development. F(2): Medium-weight euro with moderate setup and rules complexity. Ar(4): Rich medieval artwork and quality components evoke the historical period.

candidates.name: SETI: Space Agencies
mechs: VIC-01 Victory Points from Game State
VIC-02 Victory Points from Player Actions
candidates.description: Lead humanity's search for extraterrestrial intelligence through space exploration, technology development, and cosmic discovery.
candidates.justification: M(4): Deep tech trees, multi-use cards, and interlocking space agency systems. T(3): SETI theme present but mechanics feel more like optimization puzzles. G(4): Meaningful decisions in research paths and resource allocation strategies. F(2): Complex setup and rules overhead for space simulation weight. Ar(4): Clean space agency aesthetic with atmospheric cosmic imagery.

candidates.name: Ada's Dream
candidates.description: Build and program steampunk automatons alongside Ada Lovelace to solve Victorian-era puzzles and unlock mechanical wonders.
candidates.justification: M(4): Programming mechanisms with tech trees and multi-use card systems. T(3): Victorian steampunk setting pleasant but mechanics don't fully generate it. G(4): Meaningful programming decisions with cascading consequences across scenarios. F(3): Campaign setup and component management add moderate overhead. Ar(4): Elegant Victorian aesthetic with detailed steampunk machinery illustrations.
